correctness.rationale: Planar Minkowski support-measure linearity constructs K as weights (1±epsilon)/2 of two m-gons rotated by pi/m; their support values and adjacent vertex sums give precise inradius and circumradius even for endpoint zero weights. A convexity comparison F(s)=R(s)+r(s)<2 from both endpoint values proves the inward deficit dominates for all s=|epsilon|. Cell-based primal couplings to nodes, and matching geodesic 1-Lipschitz potentials, establish each exact W1 by dual equality. Uniform Taylor expansion proves dH=(pi²/(3N²))(1+3|epsilon|)+O(N^-4). Independent convex-hull Minkowski geometry across m=3,4,7,15 and 5 imbalance values matched radii and dH; these finite checks supplement analytic proof.

value.rationale: The period-two alternating grid is the simplest genuinely nonuniform balanced facet measure and naturally tests sharpness of Minkowski reconstruction stability hypotheses. A complete sharp family-wise Hausdorff and two Wasserstein formulas, including endpoint support collapse, is a useful standalone natural invariant, even though the broader qualitative possibility of order-1/N transport with order-1/N² shape was previously shown for other patterns.

final_claim: For N=2m, m>=3 and |epsilon|<=1, alternating weights (1+epsilon (-1)^j)/N on the uniform circle grid have Steiner-centered Minkowski body with exact dH=1-(pi/N)cot(pi/N)+|epsilon|(pi/N)tan(pi/N); geodesic W1 to uniform circle pi(1+epsilon^2)/(2N) and to equal grid pi|epsilon|/N, preserving quadratic Hausdorff convergence despite order 1/N measure perturbation.
limitations: Geodesic, not chordal, W1 and perimeter 2pi, Steiner-centered shapes only.
